## Structure and components

- [statement] PrintNinja describes initial custom board-game prices as budgetary and withholds a final quotation until artwork review. Treat an early estimate as provisional and ask for a written quote against the final artwork and component specification. This is its board-game quotation policy, not a universal rule for all card printers. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/custom-board-game-pricing/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol
- [statement] Loffler describes paper and staples as excluded from its explanation of click charges. Ask what consumables, parts and maintenance a proposed service rate actually covers, and price the substrate separately unless the written agreement includes it. Do not transfer this supplier description into an assumption about every contract. (low confidence) — https://www.loffler.com/blog/true-cost-of-owning-a-commercial-printer · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use the same buyer-supplied artwork for demonstrations and request the workflow through finishing. Ricoh describes start-to-finishing demonstrations, while Konica Minolta invites advance submission of the buyer’s files for printed samples. These are manufacturer offers, not independently measured results. (medium confidence) — https://www.ricoh-usa.com/en/production-printing/about/customer-experience-center · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol · also: https://kmbs.konicaminolta.us/client-engagement-center/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In a DC-618 operator discussion, Andres reports that later-cut cards have more skew, while tngcas reports replacing rollers to resolve a similar problem. Use these attributed anecdotes to challenge a demo with checks across the whole sheet and run, and to ask about roller maintenance. They do not establish defects, lifetime or failure rates for other machine models. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/duplo-dc-618-skewing-in-machine.295010/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol
- [statement] In an April 2024 PrintPlanet thread, operator COGordon reports double feeding on a Duplo 646 with lighter stock despite service-setting changes. This is a self-reported case on that model and stock class, not a measured failure rate or proof of a defect in another machine model. Use it to justify observing real-stock feeding during the demo. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/methods-for-reducing-static-on-duplo-646.294079/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Duplo says application testing produces an emailed report. Request that report and returned sample output as documentary evidence rather than accepting a verbal compatibility assurance. (low confidence) — https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol
- [statement] PrintNinja labels one published price configuration as a 54-card poker deck with a printed tuck box. Use that example only for that configuration; obtain a separate quote for the commissioned game instead of scaling an unrelated deck price. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/printing-prices/card-game-printing/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol
- [statement] Duplo’s application-testing form says laminated substrates require compatibility testing and promises an emailed results report. Request qualification of the intended finished stock rather than assuming that an accepted paper weight establishes compatibility. (low confidence) — https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol
- [statement] For an equipment quote, request a full-system cost schedule rather than relying on the press price or a demonstration calculator alone. Printing Impressions reports that finishing and landed delivery belong in ownership analysis; Konica Minolta describes its demonstration cost review as raw-cost calculators. This is a procurement recommendation, not a measured cost or break-even estimate. (medium confidence) — https://www.piworld.com/article/anatomy-determining-total-cost-ownership-production-inkjet-presses/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol · also: https://kmbs.konicaminolta.us/client-engagement-center/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Protocol recommendation: give each candidate the same real game artwork and intended substrate, and request a complete sample run through finishing. Ricoh offers start-to-finishing demonstrations, Duplo requires substrate compatibility tests, and a former equipment seller advises bringing customer files to demos. These sources support the test design; they do not demonstrate this game on any machine. (medium confidence) — https://www.ricoh-usa.com/en/production-printing/about/customer-experience-center · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol · also: https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx, https://printplanet.com/threads/new-owner-new-equipment.292427/
- [statement] PrintNinja distinguishes public example pricing from US-delivery quotes: its price table excludes shipping, sales tax and duties, while its order guide describes US quotes as including taxes and duties. Preserve both attributed statements and obtain an itemized destination-specific quote; neither supports assuming every advertised price is landed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02) — https://printninja.com/printing-prices/card-game-printing/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol · also: https://printninja.com/placing-an-order/
- [statement] Protocol recommendation: request a full-system quote covering the press and required finishing, software and service. Duplo explicitly sells the controller PC separately; Loffler lists cutting, collating, coating and laminating among finishing processes; a print-shop discussion advises confirming service and software rates. The sources provide no complete installed-system price for this game. (medium confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol · also: https://www.loffler.com/blog/true-cost-of-owning-a-commercial-printer, https://printplanet.com/threads/new-owner-new-equipment.292427/
- [statement] A production-equipment discussion recommends checking whether click charges vary by sheet size and remain fixed for the lease term; another print-shop operator recommends checking minimum-usage fees. Ask suppliers to write the charging basis and minimums into their quotes. These are historical purchasing cautions, not current market rates. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/new-owner-new-equipment.292427/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol
- [statement] Duplo publishes a maximum DC-648 speed of 40 sheets per minute. This is a manufacturer sheet-processing rating, not demonstrated finished-game output. Protocol recommendation: time the whole sample workflow, including setup and downtime, and count completed decks; Ricoh offers workflow demonstrations and Loffler identifies setup and downtime as costs. (medium confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol · also: https://www.ricoh-usa.com/en/production-printing/about/customer-experience-center, https://www.loffler.com/blog/true-cost-of-owning-a-commercial-printer
- [statement] Duplo’s DC-648 page identifies a separately sold PC Controller. Ask the written equipment quote to name the supplied controller configuration and price any required computer explicitly. (low confidence) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-648-slitter-cutter-creaser/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol
- [statement] Printing Impressions advises checking warranty and service exclusions, separate software/DFE contracts and upgrade costs before closing. Recommended quote protocol: require these coverage boundaries and recurring charges in writing. The article is historical industry reporting, not a current vendor service offer. (low confidence) — https://www.piworld.com/article/anatomy-determining-total-cost-ownership-production-inkjet-presses/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol
- [statement] Freeze card count, material, finish and packaging in the request for quote. PrintNinja’s guide explicitly asks about those specifications, and its public price examples identify a particular deck and box configuration. Treat the commissioned game configuration as a separate custom request; do not reuse an example-deck price as its quote. (medium confidence) — https://printninja.com/game-quote-guide/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol · also: https://printninja.com/printing-prices/card-game-printing/
- [statement] Recommended comparison protocol: send one unchanged job specification and identical artwork to each candidate; request returned samples and a written account of the tested stock and workflow. The basis is the vendors’ own-file demonstrations and substrate qualification, not evidence that these suppliers have already produced this game successfully. (medium confidence) — https://kmbs.konicaminolta.us/client-engagement-center/ · keywords: Print procurement quote and machine demo protocol · also: https://app.duplousa.com/contact/atr.aspx
